title: Pool acquire clears slot fd before returning — prevents double-close on concurrent cleanup — defend this
description: Why correct: pool_acquire() sets pool->slots[i].fd = -1 before releasing the lock and returning the fd to the caller. If cleanup() runs concurrently, it acquires the lock, sees fd==-1, and skips the close. The caller's fd is safe. Without this clear, cleanup could close the same fd the caller is actively using for ioctls, causing EBADF on the next ioctl — a mysterious hardware error during operation. What a contributor might change: 'why clear the fd? That looks like we lost the handle.' Answer: we haven't lost it — the fd is alive with the caller. The slot is just a lease mechanism; the fd lives independently once leased.
